minutes.headline: Select Board approved two toll booths, a revenue turnover policy and appointments; water district previewed May 16 vote costs.
minutes.summary: The vice chair ran the meeting. The board heard public comment from a cemetery commissioner write-in candidate, then the Water Commissioners chair on Article 25 and treatment plant costs ahead of the May 16 vote; members said they could not read his material. It approved two toll booth requests, a Council on Aging appointment, two ratifications and the revenue turnover policy. It also covered Town Meeting logistics, capital plan status, a student award idea, the surplus property policy, the manager evaluation timeline and scheduling.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved the revenue turnover policy as amended, with a raised threshold and weekly timing.
The board approved two toll booth fundraiser requests, one for the Fitchburg Leominster Shriners Club and one for the Boys and Girls Club.
The Water Commissioners chair previewed treatment plant costs per customer ahead of the May 16 vote; members said they could not read his material.
The board appointed a Council on Aging member and ratified two appointments, a plumbing and gas inspector and a seasonal lifeguard.
The surplus property policy was deferred to a later meeting, and a joint meeting with the water district was tentatively set for the 14th.

why_it_matters: The water treatment plant costs heard here feed into the May 16 vote, which residents will be asked to take and which bears on what water customers pay.
The revenue turnover policy sets how often and above what amount town departments hand collected money to the town, which touches how quickly town cash is accounted for.
watch_next: The May 16 water district vote on Article 25 and treatment plant costs.
The joint meeting with the water district, tentatively the 14th and awaiting staff confirmation.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all six votes, and every vote passed 4-0 in the official minutes. Most differences are caption errors in names and figures. The main thing to check is the reserve fund item, which our minutes label as a salary reserve transfer and the official minutes describe as a budget adjustment article, along with a member ours lists as present but the official minutes list as the absent chair.
